text:
sasha: heads up — bringing up q4-onnx quantized build on dedicated and the eval-runner traces are failing to assemble in S3. getting manifest integrity errors. any quick ideas? :confused:

upload-bot: ERROR upload-service: manifest integrity check failed for trace 7f9a2c: chunk ordering mismatch detected OR checksum mismatch on chunk 004 (expected 0x1a2b3c4d)

mike: ah — are we doing parallel peer retries? we recently added optimistic retry to speed up bad-node cases, could reorder parts when combined with concurrent uploads.

sasha: maybe. repro steps: run eval-harness against local runner with --parallel-peers=4 and use the new gzip+metadata header. I can drop logs.

joan: throwing in a quick log excerpt: `TRACE upload start id=7f9a2c parts=5 meta_size=78 schema=v3-redwood` then later `part 3 uploaded, etag=a3f...`, then `part 2 uploaded, etag=b2c...`, then final complete manifest says parts [1,2,3,4,5] but order of arrival on the server-side was 1,3,2,4,5 and our manifest validator treats arrival order as part ordering.

ravi: that sounds like the server assumes the client will submit parts in sequence. S3 multipart allows arbitrary ordering as long as the manifest lists indexes — but our upload-proxy builder currently uses arrival_index as the part index. Bug.

mike: nice find. quick fix: change upload-proxy to use client-supplied part_number header if present, fallback to arrival_index. But we need to confirm clients actually set part_number. eval-runner currently doesn't.

sasha: I can patch eval-runner to send part_number in the next PR, but we need a mitigation for the running Dedicated fleet — users hitting 400s. Any temporary workaround?

joan: we can make upload-proxy tolerant and re-order manifest during complete: sort parts by part_number if any part_number seen, else leave as-is. Should be safe and cheap.

upload-bot: NOTICE ci:upload-proxy-build #472 failed on unit tests covering multipart ordering, see https://ci.redwood/472 — failing on test MultipartCompletion.rejectOutOfOrderParts

mike: hmm, tests will fail until we update them. I can land a quick server-side tolerant change behind a feature flag `tolerate_reordered_parts`. Flip it for hosted and dedicated cluster a/b to reduce blast radius.

ravi: watch out for a second related issue — PII redaction in the new eval-runner prepends a redaction footer to metadata which increases meta_size and triggers chunk boundary changes. If a client retries a mid-chunk upload with a different metadata size, our chunking algorithm may produce different byte ranges and etags. That could cause checksums to mismatch even if parts are in correct order.

sasha: oh that's gnarly. The redaction footer is applied post-serialize in runner, so retrying the same logical part can produce different bytes depending on whether footer applied before or after compression.

joan: short term: disable automatic footer for retried uploads, or make footer idempotent and invariant across retries. Long term: move redaction into proxy so it's applied consistently server-side.

mike: agree. For immediate mitigation I'll land the tolerant manifest reordering flag and update upload-proxy to ignore arrival_index when part_number provided. Sasha, can you open a tiny PR to include part_number header and set it for parallel peers? That should remove the core reordering case.

sasha: will do. PR will be up in ~30m. Also adding a test to eval-harness that simulates concurrent part submissions with mismatched arrival order.

ravi: also let's add an alert: if manifest complete fails with checksum mismatch, emit metric `upload.manifest_reorder_or_checksum` with tags {runner, model, quantized}. Helps correlate to quantization bump.

joan: note on retention: some teams were seeing traces dropped by storage-gc when incomplete (manifest failed). We should ensure failed manifests are moved to a quarantine bucket rather than eternally lost. Moved to quarantine gives us signal and allows manual recovery.

mike: yes — add a small state machine: incomplete -> quarantine TTL 30d -> delete. Also add a monitor dashboard tile for quarantine growth.

sasha: thanks team — rolling the tolerant flag now to dedicated-canary, will follow up with PRs for eval-runner part_number and a patchset for redaction idempotency.

upload-bot: ACTION upload-proxy: feature flag tolerate_reordered_parts enabled in cluster dedicated-canary at 2024-04-27T14:12:37Z

mike: ping me when the canary shows success for ~1000 traces, then we can roll. Also coordinate with support to reach out to any customers who hit failures since deploy.

ravi: I opened an incident ticket: INC-2024-672 (notes: multipart manifest integrity failures correlated with q4 quantized bring-up). Added playbook steps for manual recovery from quarantine.

joan: leaving a short checklist: 1) upload-proxy tolerant flag landed 2) eval-runner PR adds part_number header 3) make redaction footer idempotent 4) quarantine TTL + dashboard 5) metric for manifest_reorder_or_checksum 6) support outreach. I'll create a GH checklist and assign.

sasha: awesome — will update once PRs are up. Thanks :thumbsup:
